1.explanation: DrilldownOverlayBehavior.js is responsible for adding and removing the deep-link overlay button based on whether a collapsed subprocess plane exists. It uses getPlaneIdFromShape (in DrilldownUtil.js) to find the matching plane. SubprocessCompatibility.js is the multi-diagram plugin that, upon import, creates new BPMNPlane elements for collapsed subprocesses but does not assign them the IDs (with the “_plane” suffix) that DrilldownUtil expects. Because the newly created plane IDs don’t match getPlaneIdFromShape, DrilldownOverlayBehavior.canDrillDown() returns false and the arrow overlay is never re-added. Adjusting SubprocessCompatibility to set the correct plane IDs (or adapting DrilldownUtil to discover planes by businessObject) will keep the overlay intact after drill-down.
1.bug_scenario: In the provided animation the user starts at the root process, collapses a subprocess and sees the little “down-arrow” overlay (deep-link) on it. Clicking the arrow drills into the subprocess as expected. However, because the multi-diagram plugin (SubprocessCompatibility) creates a new BPMNPlane for that subprocess, the deep-link overlay is never re-attached in the new view. As a result, once you arrive in the subprocess plane, the overlay is lost and you can no longer drill back or see the arrow on nested subprocesses.
